title: Big and bigger
caption: Visitors beside the Auxiliary Telescopes and a Unit Telescope of the Very Large Telescope at sunset, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A small crowd gathers by the telescopes at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile to watch the night arrive. For most people sunset ends the working day, but here the real work begins after dark, under a clear sky.

The people look tiny next to the domes on their left. These house the four 1.8-meter Auxiliary Telescopes of the Very Large Telescope array. The biggest structure in the picture is at the far left, a VLT Unit Telescope, which makes the crowd look like ants. The VLT has four of these 8.2-meter telescopes, some of the largest on the planet.

ESO planned to go bigger still with the European Extremely Large Telescope, then expected to see first light in the early 2020s. Its mirror is designed to be 39 meters across, which the source describes as bigger and better eyes on the sky.
